caption: What if you aged backwards like the immortal jellyfish? Turritopsis dohrnii is only about 4.5 mm wide, smaller than your pinky nail. Most jellies start life as a polyp stuck to a rock, bud off swimming jellies, grow up and die. But if this one is hurt or starving, it sinks, shrinks into a blob and turns back into a polyp, like dadaji turning back into a baby. Its cells switch jobs, one kind becoming another, which scientists call transdifferentiation. The new polyp then buds many jellies with the same genes. In a 2009 study in Japan, lab jellies rewound their lives four times. It has no brain or heart, it's about 95% water, and fish still eat it, so 'immortal' just means it can restart. Humans can't do this. Plot twist: in the 1980s, a student forgot some jellies in a lab jar and came back to find polyps instead. If YOU could restart, which age would you pick? 👇
